BRIGHT SPARKS JUNIOR SCHOOL PREPARES FOR TERM III REOPENING AFTER A SUCCESSFUL TERM II

P.7 Candidates to report on 7th September, 2026 while all other continuing classes (KG-P6) are expected to report on 14th September, 2026

By Bright Sparks Junior School
School Communications Office
Published Sep 4, 2026, 9:00 AM EAT Updated Sep 4, 2026, 1:21 PM EAT

Academics — Bright Sparks Junior School, Kampala

SEGUKU, WAKISO   As Term II 2026 comes to an official close, Bright Sparks Junior School has announced comprehensive updates for all parents, guardians, and pupils regarding academic achievements, co-curricular developments, and key schedules for Term III.
In a school-wide circular issued by the Office of the Head Teacher, the administration expressed appreciation to the entire parent community for their trust and financial partnership, which allowed all institutional activities to run seamlessly throughout the term.

Academic Progress & Curriculum Coverage

Term II has seen strong academic performance and structured learning across all class levels:
  1. Candidate Class (P.7): Syllabuses across all subjects were fully completed. P.7 pupils wrote four comprehensive sets of Mock examinations (two internal assessments, WAPSSHA Mocks, and SUREKEY Examination Board Special Mock) followed by an intensive two-week remediation and concept clearance workshop.
  2. Continuing Classes (Kindergarten to P.6): Detailed progress reports have been compiled and issued. Parents are encouraged to review these reports with their children and support disciplined revision during the holiday break.

Co-Curricular Highlights & Educational Tours

Bright Sparks Junior School continued its commitment to holistic child development with significant achievements outside the classroom:
Wakiso District Primary Schools Ball Games: The school sports teams proudly represented Bright Sparks, competing up to the cluster level.
Academic & Clubs Exhibition Day: Held on Saturday, July 11, 2026, in the Main Dining Hall, the event featured project displays from various student clubs, entertainment by KTA, and delicious showcases from the Bakery Club.
Albertine Region Study Trip: Learners from Primary 5, Primary 6, and Primary 7 completed an enriching 4-day study trip to the Albertine Region, exploring geographical landmarks, ecological sites, and national oil exploration infrastructure.
Term III Reporting Schedule & Key Dates
To maximize candidate preparation while allowing continuing pupils adequate rest, the school has set a staggered opening schedule for Term III 2026:
DateEven/MilestoneTarget Group
7th September, 2026Early Reporting & Resumtion of ClassesP.7 Candidates
14th September, 2026Official Opening of Term IIIContinuing Classes (KG-P.6
26th September, 2026P.7 Leaver's PartyP.7 Candidates
24th October, 2026Academic DayAll Classes & Parents
30th-31st October, 2026P.7 Candidates' Dedication DayP.7 Candidates & Families

Financial Guidelines for Term III

School management reminds all parents that Term III is the final and briefest term of the academic year. A strict fee policy requires 100% clearance of school fees prior to learners accessing school premises. Parents with pending obligations are advised to engage the Bursar’s Office before the opening dates to ensure smooth entry and uninterrupted learning.
Head Teacher Muneeb Ali Wanyeni wished all Bright Sparks families a restful, safe, and productive holiday break as preparations continue for a successful Term III.
